mcq.q: Nutrient-poor, free-draining soils often give higher wine quality because they
choices: A Always hold more water than clay
B Limit vigour so the vine sets a smaller, riper crop
C Force the grower to irrigate with seawater
mcq.answer: B Limit vigour so the vine sets a smaller, riper crop
mcq.why: Gravel, granite and slate starve the vine of easy water and nitrogen.

mcq.q: The Humboldt and Benguela currents matter to coastal Chile and South Africa because they
choices: A Heat the coast like the Gulf Stream in Bordeaux
B Cool the coast with cold water and often fog
C Create noble rot every year
D Bring monsoon rain in January
mcq.answer: B Cool the coast with cold water and often fog
mcq.why: Cold currents are a New World cool-climate tool.

mcq.q: Leafroll virus is a problem because it
choices: A Improves colour in every red grape
B Delays ripening and can reduce colour and yield
D Replaces the need for rootstocks
mcq.answer: B Delays ripening and can reduce colour and yield
mcq.why: A widespread vine virus; planting certified material is the control.

mcq.q: Cane pruning (for example Guyot) leaves
choices: A Only a head of two-bud spurs on a bush
B One or two canes of many buds tied to a wire
mcq.answer: B One or two canes of many buds tied to a wire
mcq.why: Guyot is the classic cane system of Burgundy and much of Bordeaux.

mcq.q: A cool ferment for a thiol-driven Sauvignon Blanc is typically in the region of
choices: D No temperature control at all
mcq.answer: B About 12–16 °C in stainless steel
mcq.why: Cool, reductive ferments protect passion-fruit and boxwood notes.

mcq.q: Micro-oxygenation is used on some reds to
choices: B Soften tannin and stabilise colour with a measured oxygen dose in tank
C Replace the need for any SO2 in every wine
mcq.answer: B Soften tannin and stabilise colour with a measured oxygen dose in tank
mcq.why: A tank substitute for some of the effects of barrel ageing; easy to overdo.

mcq.q: Residual sugar in a still wine can legally and practically come from
choices: B Stopping ferment, blending in unfermented must (süssreserve), or fortifying
mcq.answer: B Stopping ferment, blending in unfermented must (süssreserve), or fortifying
mcq.why: Know the three still-wine routes; fortification is the fortified-wine route.

mcq.q: Settling or flotation of white juice before ferment is done to
choices: A Increase solids to the maximum
B Reduce solids so the ferment is cleaner and less phenolic
mcq.answer: B Reduce solids so the ferment is cleaner and less phenolic
mcq.why: Too many solids give bitterness and reduction; a little fine lees can be kept.

mcq.q: Listrac and Moulis are
choices: B Inland Haut-Médoc village AOCs, usually a little less famous than the riverside four
mcq.answer: B Inland Haut-Médoc village AOCs, usually a little less famous than the riverside four
mcq.why: They sit on plateaux away from the Gironde; more clay in Listrac.

mcq.q: Sainte-Foy-Bordeaux and Graves de Vayres are examples of
choices: B Lesser-known Bordeaux AOCs for red and/or white wines
mcq.answer: B Lesser-known Bordeaux AOCs for red and/or white wines
mcq.why: The Bordeaux map is wider than Médoc and Saint-Émilion.

mcq.q: Volnay, compared with Pommard, is often described as
choices: A The more robust, tannic Côte de Beaune red
B The more fragrant, lighter Côte de Beaune red
mcq.answer: B The more fragrant, lighter Côte de Beaune red
mcq.why: Two neighbouring Beaune red villages; Pommard is the firmer stereotype.

mcq.q: Irancy is a northerly Burgundy AOC for
choices: B Pinot Noir (with a little César allowed) near Chablis
mcq.answer: B Pinot Noir (with a little César allowed) near Chablis
mcq.why: A rare red outpost in the Yonne.

mcq.q: Anjou rouge is typically
choices: B Cabernet Franc and/or Cabernet Sauvignon, often a touch riper than Touraine
mcq.answer: B Cabernet Franc and/or Cabernet Sauvignon, often a touch riper than Touraine
mcq.why: Anjou-Villages is the quality red tier; whites split Anjou Blanc and the sweet Layon.

mcq.q: Montlouis-sur-Loire, facing Vouvray, is also
choices: B A Chenin Blanc AOC (still and sparkling) on the south bank of the Loire
D A Priorat vi de vila
mcq.answer: B A Chenin Blanc AOC (still and sparkling) on the south bank of the Loire
mcq.why: Same grape, similar styles; a slightly different soil story.

mcq.q: Crozes-Hermitage blanc is made from
mcq.answer: B Marsanne and/or Roussanne
mcq.why: The same white pair as Hermitage blanc; volume is higher and quality more mixed.

mcq.q: Rasteau as a still red (not the VDN) is
choices: B A Southern Rhône village red, Grenache-based, from a warm site
mcq.answer: B A Southern Rhône village red, Grenache-based, from a warm site
mcq.why: Like Beaumes-de-Venise, the village has both a dry red AOC and a fortified AOC.

mcq.q: Jurançon is a Pyrenean AOC for
choices: A Dry and sweet wines from Petit and Gros Manseng
mcq.answer: A Dry and sweet wines from Petit and Gros Manseng
mcq.why: Late-harvest passerillage sweets and punchy dry whites; not Sauternes grapes.

mcq.q: Alsace Crémant is a sparkling wine; still Alsace Pinot Blanc is often used for
choices: B Everyday still wine and as a base for Crémant d’Alsace
mcq.answer: B Everyday still wine and as a base for Crémant d’Alsace
mcq.why: Pinot Blanc / Auxerrois is the workhorse; Grand Cru is not its usual home.

mcq.q: Langhe Nebbiolo on a label is usually
choices: B A more approachable, shorter-aged Nebbiolo from a wider Piedmont zone than Barolo
mcq.answer: B A more approachable, shorter-aged Nebbiolo from a wider Piedmont zone than Barolo
mcq.why: Declassified or younger-vine fruit; same grape, less time, lower price.

mcq.q: Sant’Antimo and IGT Toscana are often the legal homes of
choices: B International blends that do not fit Chianti or Brunello rules (Super Tuscans)
mcq.answer: B International blends that do not fit Chianti or Brunello rules (Super Tuscans)
mcq.why: The Super Tuscan story is a legal-category story as much as a grape story.

mcq.q: Valpolicella Classico, without Ripasso or Amarone, is typically
choices: B A light to medium, cherry-fruited dry red for early drinking
mcq.answer: B A light to medium, cherry-fruited dry red for early drinking
mcq.why: Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella; the everyday wine of the hills.

mcq.q: Sicily’s Nero d’Avola, in a warm lowland site, tends to be
choices: A As pale and tannic as Barolo
B Ripe, medium-full, dark-fruited; altitude or sea breeze keeps it from jam
mcq.answer: B Ripe, medium-full, dark-fruited; altitude or sea breeze keeps it from jam
mcq.why: Etna is a different, cooler story (Nerello); do not merge them.

mcq.q: Montsant encircles much of Priorat and offers
choices: B Similar Garnacha/Cariñena reds, usually a little less extreme in price and extraction
mcq.answer: B Similar Garnacha/Cariñena reds, usually a little less extreme in price and extraction
mcq.why: A DO in its own right; a logical tasting neighbour to Priorat.

mcq.q: Godello from Valdeorras is a
choices: B Fuller dry white from Galicia, more stone-fruit and body than many Albariños
mcq.answer: B Fuller dry white from Galicia, more stone-fruit and body than many Albariños
mcq.why: Inland Galicia; also Bierzo whites.

mcq.q: Cigales is a Castilian DO historically known for
choices: B Rosado and, increasingly, Tempranillo reds
mcq.answer: B Rosado and, increasingly, Tempranillo reds
mcq.why: On the Duero axis with Ribera and Toro.

mcq.q: Kamptal and Kremstal DAC wines of note are mainly
mcq.answer: B Grüner Veltliner and Riesling
mcq.why: Danube neighbours of the Wachau; loess and rock, Heiligenstein etc.

mcq.q: Tokaji Szamorodni is
choices: B A wine from bunches with a mix of healthy and aszú berries, which may be dry or sweet
mcq.answer: B A wine from bunches with a mix of healthy and aszú berries, which may be dry or sweet
mcq.why: The ‘as it comes’ wine; Aszú is the selected berry wine.

mcq.q: Palmela and the Península de Setúbal produce
choices: B Castelão reds and the fortified Moscatel de Setúbal
mcq.answer: B Castelão reds and the fortified Moscatel de Setúbal
mcq.why: Sandy/clay south of Lisbon; two different products from one peninsula.

mcq.q: Alvarinho in Portugal and Albariño in Spain are
choices: B The same variety, on two sides of the Minho
mcq.answer: B The same variety, on two sides of the Minho
mcq.why: Monção/Melgaço vs Rías Baixas: a cross-border grape.

mcq.q: Carneros AVA, at the south of Napa and Sonoma, is cooled by
choices: B San Pablo Bay wind and fog, and is planted to Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
mcq.answer: B San Pablo Bay wind and fog, and is planted to Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
mcq.why: A shared cool bay AVA; sparkling houses also buy fruit here.

mcq.q: Carmenère in Chile is typically
choices: B A late-ripening red that needs a warm site or it tastes green
mcq.answer: B A late-ripening red that needs a warm site or it tastes green
mcq.why: Once mixed up with Merlot; ripe it is spicy and dark; unripe it is herbal.

mcq.q: Tasmania’s still wines, besides sparkling base, are mainly
choices: B Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, plus some aromatic whites, in a cool climate
mcq.answer: B Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, plus some aromatic whites, in a cool climate
mcq.why: Cool island; also Riesling and Pinot Gris in places.

mcq.q: Marlborough sub-zones Awatere and Wairau differ in that
choices: A Awatere is typically cooler, windier and more herbaceous in Sauvignon Blanc
B Awatere is a warm Cabernet basin
C Both are Central Otago Pinot zones
mcq.answer: A Awatere is typically cooler, windier and more herbaceous in Sauvignon Blanc
mcq.why: Wairau is the original, slightly riper valley; Awatere is more austere.

mcq.q: An Australian GI (for example Barossa Valley) on a label generally requires
mcq.answer: B 85% from that GI
mcq.why: 85% is the usual Australian claim for GI, variety and vintage.

mcq.q: New Zealand’s geographic claims on labels typically require
choices: A 75% from the named region and variety
B 85% from the named region and variety
mcq.answer: B 85% from the named region and variety
mcq.why: Aligned with the 85% idea used in Australia and the EU.

mcq.q: A wine can be labelled with a vintage in the EU only if
choices: A At least 85% of the grapes are from that year (unless a stricter local rule)
mcq.answer: A At least 85% of the grapes are from that year (unless a stricter local rule)
mcq.why: The same 85% idea as a stated variety.

mcq.q: Pinot Noir in Champagne is used for
choices: B Body and red-fruit character in blends, and for Blanc de Noirs and rosé
mcq.answer: B Body and red-fruit character in blends, and for Blanc de Noirs and rosé
mcq.why: Montagne de Reims and the Côte des Bar are the Pinot strongholds.

mcq.q: Gyropalettes exist to
choices: B Automate riddling of traditional-method bottles
mcq.answer: B Automate riddling of traditional-method bottles
mcq.why: A cage of bottles is rotated by machine instead of hand remuage.

mcq.q: Franciacorta Satèn is
choices: B A Blanc de Blancs-style, lower-pressure Franciacorta
mcq.answer: B A Blanc de Blancs-style, lower-pressure Franciacorta
mcq.why: Chardonnay (and Pinot Bianco); silkier mousse by law.

mcq.q: California traditional-method wines often come from
choices: A Only the hottest Central Valley floor
B Cooler sites such as Carneros, Anderson Valley or the Sonoma Coast
mcq.answer: B Cooler sites such as Carneros, Anderson Valley or the Sonoma Coast
mcq.why: Houses historically used Champagne grapes in bay- and coast-cooled AVAs.

mcq.q: A sparkling wine labelled Doux is
choices: B The sweetest EU band (over 50 g/L)
D A synonym of Brut Nature
mcq.answer: B The sweetest EU band (over 50 g/L)
mcq.why: Rare; a dessert sparkler.

mcq.q: Manzanilla Pasada is
choices: B An older Manzanilla that has begun to lose flor and take on a slightly oxidative note
mcq.answer: B An older Manzanilla that has begun to lose flor and take on a slightly oxidative note
mcq.why: A step toward amontillado while still a Sanlúcar wine.

mcq.q: White Port and tonic is a service idea that suits
choices: B A chilled, relatively inexpensive white Port as an aperitif
mcq.answer: B A chilled, relatively inexpensive white Port as an aperitif
mcq.why: Long drink over ice; not a use for a declared vintage.

mcq.q: Canteiro ageing on Madeira means
choices: A A hot tank for three months only
B Cask ageing in a warm loft for years, used for better wines
mcq.answer: B Cask ageing in a warm loft for years, used for better wines
mcq.why: The quality path versus estufagem.

mcq.q: Muscat de Frontignan and other Languedoc Muscat VDNs are
choices: B Sweet fortified Muscats, usually youthful and grapey if bottled early
mcq.answer: B Sweet fortified Muscats, usually youthful and grapey if bottled early
mcq.why: A family with Beaumes-de-Venise; climate is warm Mediterranean.

mcq.q: A Rutherglen Muscat classified as Rare is
choices: B The oldest, most concentrated commercial tier
mcq.answer: B The oldest, most concentrated commercial tier
mcq.why: Rutherglen → Classic → Grand → Rare is the richness ladder.

mcq.q: A ‘tired’ wine on the SAT development scale is
choices: B Past its best, with fading fruit
C A quality score of Outstanding
mcq.answer: B Past its best, with fading fruit
mcq.why: Development: youthful / developing / fully developed / tired.

mcq.q: Old wines with sediment should be stood upright before service so that
choices: A The cork dries out completely
B The crust drops to the bottom, making decanting cleaner
mcq.answer: B The crust drops to the bottom, making decanting cleaner
mcq.why: Then pull the cork gently and pour in one motion against a light.

mcq.q: Protein-rich, fatty red meat is a classic match for
choices: B A tannic, full-bodied red whose tannin is bound by the protein and fat
C A delicate off-dry Riesling only
mcq.answer: B A tannic, full-bodied red whose tannin is bound by the protein and fat
mcq.why: The structural match; sauce and spice still need a second look.

mcq.q: Balance on the SAT quality grid means
choices: A The taster likes the wine
B No one component (acid, tannin, alcohol, sugar, oak) sticks out unpleasantly
mcq.answer: B No one component (acid, tannin, alcohol, sugar, oak) sticks out unpleasantly
mcq.why: BLIC: balance, length, intensity, complexity.

parts.prompt: For Barossa Valley, Hunter Valley, Coonawarra and Margaret River, state climate, signature grape(s) and a style point.
points: Barossa: warm, sheltered; old-vine Shiraz; full, ripe, often American or French oak.
Hunter: humid, mesoclimate; Semillon (early pick, bottle age) and some Shiraz; moderate alcohol Semillon is the classic.
Coonawarra: moderate, Terra rossa over limestone; Cabernet; mint/eucalypt debate, cassis, firm.
Margaret River: maritime; Cabernet and Chardonnay; structured, Bordeaux/Burgundy-minded.
One extra accurate GI (Clare Riesling, Yarra Pinot, McLaren Grenache) can replace a thin answer.
Do not invent GIs.

parts.prompt: Why can Hunter Semillon be picked at low potential alcohol and still become a complex wine?
points: High acid at early pick; flavour is lemon/grass, not fat tropical.
Little or no oak; the complexity is from bottle age (toast, honey, wax).
Humidity makes later picking risky (rot).
Screwcap has helped a 10–20 year path.
It is a local technique, not a copy of oaked Barossa Semillon (uncommon anyway).
Contrast with ripe oaked Hunter Chardonnay if mentioned.

parts.prompt: Outline winery choices for a premium Barossa Shiraz versus a Clare Valley dry Riesling.
points: Shiraz: ripe fruit, open fermenters, plunge, MLF, 15–24 months oak (American traditional, French also), full body.
Riesling: early-ripe, cool tank, dry, no MLF, no new oak, sterile-stable, bottle age optional.
Both: clean fruit; Clare frost and spring winds as vineyard notes can score.
Do not ferment Riesling on skins for weeks as if it were a red.
State drink windows.

parts.prompt: Describe the Valpolicella pyramid from everyday Classico to Recioto, including Ripasso and Amarone.
points: Grapes: Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella (± Molinara, others).
Valpolicella / Classico: dry, light-medium, early.
Ripasso: referment on Amarone (or Recioto) pomace — more body, alcohol, colour.
Amarone: appassimento, then ferment dry, high alcohol, full, bitter-cherry/fig.
Recioto: appassimento, residual sugar, the historic sweet wine.
Classico and Valpantena as geographic mentions; ripasso is a method, not a zone.

parts.prompt: What vineyard and drying conditions does appassimento need, and what can go wrong?
points: Healthy, ripe, loose bunches; often hillside Classico fruit.
Lofts (fruttaio), air flow, weeks to months of drying; water loss concentrates sugar and flavour.
Noble or clean dry; grey rot and volatile acidity are the risks.
Labour and loss of volume — hence price.
Warm, wet autumns are dangerous.
Botrytis is not the aim here (unlike Sauternes).

parts.prompt: Contrast Soave Classico winery practice with that of a high-volume Soave from the plain.
points: Classico: Garganega, lower yield, sometimes oak or long lees, more dry extract, can age.
Plain: higher yield, machine, cool tank, early bottling, simple pear/citrus, drink now.
Trebbiano di Soave / Chardonnay as minor partners.
Soave Superiore as a DOCG quality mention can score.
Do not describe Soave as Pinot Grigio.

written.title: Question 3 — English sparkling and New World traditional method

parts.prompt: Why is southern England able to produce traditional-method wines in a Champagne mould?
points: Cool climate, high acid, modest sugar — ideal base wines.
Chalk and green-sand in Sussex, Kent, Hampshire.
Same three grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier.
Climate change has improved ripeness in the last decades.
Still high vintage variation, frost and rain risk.
Cost of land is lower than the Côte des Blancs but yields are low.

parts.prompt: Compare an English Blanc de Blancs with a warm-climate New World bottle-fermented Chardonnay/Pinot wine.
points: English: leaner, higher acid, more citrus/green apple, may need dosage or time.
Warmer New World (some California, South Africa, Australia except Tasmania): riper fruit, lower acid unless picked early or from a cool pocket.
Tasmania, Anderson Valley, Walker Bay as cool New World exceptions.
Lees time and dosage still apply in both.
Both are traditional method if labelled as such (Cap Classique, etc.).
Do not call English wine Champagne.

parts.prompt: Give vineyard risks in England and one winery choice that can compensate for a cool, wet year.
points: Frost, poor flowering, rain at harvest, rot, low yield, underripe tannin if red grapes are used for rosé.
Compensation: earlier pick for health not sugar, chaptalisation of base wine if allowed, blending reserve wines, higher dosage, longer lees to add body, reject poor lots.
Sorting and gentle press (low phenolics).
MLF can soften acid in a very sharp year.
You cannot invent sunshine in the cellar — selection is the real tool.

written.title: Question 4 — Vintage Port production and ageing

parts.prompt: Describe the making of Vintage Port from harvest to the second winter.
points: Schist terraces, best grapes in a declared year (or a single quinta).
Foot trod or robotic lagares: fast colour and tannin in a short ferment.
Fortify to about 19–22% while sugar remains; separate from skins.
Winter in the Douro then ship down to Vila Nova de Gaia traditionally (many now age up-river).
About two years in wood; bottled unfiltered.
General declaration is a house decision, not automatic every good year.

parts.prompt: How does bottle ageing change Vintage Port, and how should a 20-year-old bottle be served?
points: Primary black fruit becomes dried fruit, spice, leather; tannin polymerises; a crust forms.
Stand up 24 hours or more; decant off sediment; serve about 16 °C in a reasonably large glass.
Drink the bottle the same day once opened (it fades faster than tawny).
Do not treat it like a 10-year tawny that lasts weeks.
Store lying down, cool and dark, until you plan to drink it.
A young vintage may be aerated longer; an old one can be fragile.

parts.prompt: Contrast Vintage Port with LBV and with 20-year Tawny in one sentence each, then pair Vintage Port with food.
points: LBV: same year, longer wood (4–6 years), usually ready, less bottle age needed.
20-year tawny: oxidative wood blend, nutty, no crust, serve cooler.
Vintage + mature blue cheese or dark chocolate; sweetness and salt.
Avoid chilli-hot food (alcohol) and a drier wine than the dish.
Award for mentioning crusted or colheita as further contrasts.
